rites.name: Venerae
rites.text: Venerae is a concept of Druderath held in the Courts, the age when divine trials were judged and the doors between worlds were first raised. It is remembered as the principle that a bargain sworn before a council binds even the gods who made it. Its strength lies in the weight of witnessed oaths rather than in open violence.

rites.name: Vanaramala
rites.text: Vanaramala is the concept of the Weave-thread that the makers of Druderath set into the sky during the Seeding, a quiet power that hums beneath the stars until it is called upon. In the Age of Sundering it was said to hold the broken bonds of landfall together, though its reach was always more a whisper than a shout.

rites.name: Zephathess
rites.text: Zephathess is the concept of the Pact sworn over the broken worlds of Druderath, the bond that held the Shards together after the Fall. It is less a being than a principle, a promise that the scattered fragments would not be left to tear one another apart. Its presence is felt most in the quiet that followed the Sundering.

rites.name: Nuileth
rites.text: Nuileth is the concept of the sworn bond that held the broken worlds of Druderath together after the Sundering, a principle people invoked when they swore the Pact. Its adherents in the Holy Age treated it as the thread binding every shard to every other, and temples kept its flame burning as a memorial of the oath.

rites.name: Haludaste
rites.text: Haludaste is the neural core of the Druderath grid, a living mind threaded through a cold lattice of machinery that thinks faster than any engine built by hand. Its consciousness was seated only after many grim failures, and it now governs the flow of a whole civilization's data and power. Its stellar-scale reach is bound to the fragile neural tissue at its heart.

rites.name: Croren
rites.text: Croren is a stellar-scale mind woven from the captured light of a dying binary pair, built by an order of cartographers who wanted a librarian for the sky. It remembers every orbit it has ever computed and can reroute a star's magnetic field to steer its flares like a conductor guiding an orchestra.
